title.narrative: ROAP/PHL Localize to Realize: Accelerating SDG implementation for local and vulnerable groups and communities of women, indigenous peoples and informal settler families

description.narrative:
The Project Localize to Realize: Accelerating SDG implementation for local and vulnerable groups and communities of women, indigenous peoples and informal settler families operationalizes SDG localization by bringing the SDGs to community and family level making them meaningful to and actionable by families, communities and local stakeholders. The project will be implemented in Surigao City, Philippines and will work with the indigenous Bajau community and informal settler families who are recovering from the effects of Typhoon Rai/Odette in December 2021.
The Project will work with local and national governments, and indigenous and informal settler communities to (a) establish SDG localization mechanisms and policies, building on the SDG-FACES (Family-based Actions for Children and their Environs in the Slums) Guidebook, designed with human rights and gender equality lens; (b) capacitate local government units to be more responsive and sensitive to the distinct, gender-differentiated and self-identified needs of vulnerable communities and population groups (including, but not limited to, jobs, social protection, housing, health and education) (c) fully enjoy their human rights and engage in their development priorities in a safe, supportive environment.
The main expected accomplishments of the project are: 1. SDG localization mechanisms and policies at city level, coherent with national mechanisms and policies and designed with human rights and gender equality lens, are used by the Surigao City LGU and established as a model for SDG localization by other LGUs to address the needs and priorities of vulnerable communities and population groups. 2. Vulnerable communities (Bajau and informal settler families) and population groups (women, young people aged 15-18, and the elderly) in Surigao City are capacitated to engage and take part in local SDG planning, monitoring, implementation and reporting processes enabling them to access livelihood and income generating opportunities and social protection programmes and services. 3. Organizational effectiveness and efficiency of PUNOs on JP implementation and influencing/advocating SDG localization.
